what.deliverable: One local page that shows the opportunity bank, the connection graph and the catalogue of an analyzed collection, built from the output of `eureka run`.

how.approach: Static HTML, CSS and JavaScript files written by Python. No framework. No network call. Deterministic output: two builds from the same run folder are byte-identical.

steps.action: Read the output of `mos-brand context` for the hub job and the UI-SPEC copy deck before any page work.
Write the hub files from the packet assets and tokens. Cite the book segment for every design choice.
Run `mos-brand review` on the built page and on rendered snapshots. Then a person looks at five widths.
List every item where the book is silent as a proposed segment and return the list to the book.

why.purpose: A user who ran `eureka run` needs one local page to review ranked pairs, without any data leaving the machine.
why.evidence: The 2026-10-23 review of the JHTV Fast Forward run, and the existing hub pages that were built by hand outside this repository.
why.success: `mos-brand review` passes on the hub page. Every claim and every opportunity shows "candidate, not verified" and a source link. A person approves before anything publishes.

jtbd.when: I have run Eureka on a folder of sources and hold ranked pairs in files
jtbd.want: open one local page that shows the opportunity bank, the connection graph and the catalogue
jtbd.so: I can decide which pairs deserve a human look, and no data leaves my computer
